note: Teacher readiness guidance by skill family. This augments, and never replaces, lesson content.

minutes45: 5 min · Do Now and prerequisite check
10 min · Model the core idea with a visual
10 min · Guided practice and academic talk
5 min · Exit ticket and evidence sort
minutes90: 10 min · Do Now, vocabulary, and prerequisite check
15 min · Explicit model and worked example
15 min · Guided practice with WIDA/TWR supports
20 min · Partner investigation or interactive lesson
10 min · Exit ticket, reflection, and next-day groups

numberTheory.materials: Factor-tree template, multiplication chart, colored pencils, guided notes
numberTheory.prerequisite: Recall multiplication facts and identify factor pairs.
numberTheory.misconception: Students stop a factor tree before every branch ends in a prime number.
numberTheory.responseMove: Circle each prime leaf, continue splitting composite leaves, then multiply the leaves to verify the original number.
numberTheory.successCriteria: I break a composite number into prime factors, write the product with exponents, and multiply to check it.

decimals.materials: Place-value chart, dry-erase board, guided notes
decimals.prerequisite: Read and compare place values through hundredths.
decimals.misconception: Students align digits instead of decimal points.
decimals.responseMove: Rebuild both numbers in a place-value chart and add placeholder zeros.
decimals.successCriteria: I align place values, compute accurately, and check whether the decimal answer is reasonable.

fractions.materials: Fraction bars or area models, guided notes
fractions.prerequisite: Identify numerator, denominator, and equivalent fractions.
fractions.misconception: Students divide straight across or invert the wrong number.
fractions.responseMove: Model how many groups fit before connecting the model to multiply by the reciprocal.
fractions.successCriteria: I represent the division, use the reciprocal correctly, and interpret the quotient.

ratios.materials: Ratio table, tape diagram, two-color counters
ratios.prerequisite: Multiply and divide whole numbers fluently.
ratios.misconception: Students change only one quantity when scaling a ratio.
ratios.responseMove: Color-code both quantities and label the same scale factor on each row.
ratios.successCriteria: I scale both quantities by the same factor and explain the comparison.

percents.materials: Double number line, 100-grid, calculator when appropriate
percents.prerequisite: Connect fractions and decimals to parts of 100.
percents.misconception: Students confuse a rate with the total or apply a percent to the wrong quantity.
percents.responseMove: Label the whole first, then mark the part on a double number line or 100-grid.
percents.successCriteria: I identify the whole, find the rate or percent, and justify the comparison.

expressions.materials: Expression cards, substitution organizer, guided notes
expressions.prerequisite: Use the order of operations with numerical expressions.
expressions.misconception: Students treat adjacent terms as one number or ignore operation order.
expressions.responseMove: Box each term and annotate the operation completed at each step.
expressions.successCriteria: I substitute carefully, follow operation order, and show why two expressions match.

equations.materials: Balance model, algebra tiles or counters, number line
equations.misconception: Students change one side of an equation without changing the other.
equations.responseMove: Use a balance model and narrate doing the same operation to both sides.
equations.successCriteria: I isolate the variable, keep both sides balanced, and check my solution.

statistics.materials: Data display, sticky notes or dot-plot cards, calculator
statistics.prerequisite: Order values and calculate with whole numbers and decimals.
statistics.misconception: Students choose a measure without considering distribution shape or outliers.
statistics.responseMove: Mark the center and spread on the display before selecting a measure.
statistics.successCriteria: I describe shape, center, and spread and use evidence from the display.

integers.materials: Horizontal and vertical number lines, coordinate grid
integers.prerequisite: Locate positive numbers and ordered pairs in Quadrant I.
integers.misconception: Students treat absolute value as a negative sign or reverse x and y.
integers.responseMove: Trace from zero on a number line and rehearse x first, then y on the grid.
integers.successCriteria: I use signs correctly, locate values or points, and explain distance from zero.

geometry.materials: Grid paper, ruler, shape cutouts, formula reference
geometry.prerequisite: Multiply and identify base and perpendicular height.
geometry.misconception: Students use a slanted side as height or double-count overlapping regions.
geometry.responseMove: Draw the perpendicular height and color each non-overlapping component once.
geometry.successCriteria: I identify needed dimensions, select a formula, and label square units.

volume.materials: Unit cubes, prism model, nets, formula reference
volume.prerequisite: Find rectangle area and multiply three factors.
volume.misconception: Students mix surface area and volume units or omit faces from a net.
volume.responseMove: Connect one cube layer to base area, then trace and check every face on the net.
volume.successCriteria: I choose volume or surface area, include every dimension or face, and label units.

general.materials: Worked example, visual model, guided notes
general.prerequisite: Read the problem, identify known information, and choose an operation.
general.misconception: Students start computing before identifying what the problem asks.
general.responseMove: Restate the question, annotate knowns, and choose a representation before calculating.
general.successCriteria: I solve, show a model, explain my reasoning, and check that the answer makes sense.
